item.title: Fonds Podiumkunsten: Foreign Performances or Concerts in the Netherlands (round 4, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Podiumkunsten (Performing Arts Fund NL)

Location: Activity must take place in the Netherlands. Applicants from Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Sint Maarten, Saba and Sint Eustatius are also in scope. No city or region restriction.

Award: Maximum EUR 25,000 per production, capped at EUR 75,000 for an applicant presenting multiple productions. Calculated on travel and transport costs of the foreign artists and their production only. EUR 267,500 available per round shared across this scheme and two sibling internationalisation schemes. Fees, venue and production costs stay with the applicant. No application fee.

Duration: Single performances or a short run of concerts within one programme or festival edition.

Deadline: 23 Sep 2026

Fonds Podiumkunsten's route for Dutch festivals and venues bringing in exceptional foreign performing arts and concerts that Dutch audiences would otherwise not see. The applicant must be a Netherlands-registered legal entity running a venue or festival and carrying artistic and financial responsibility for its own programme, so individuals and sole traders cannot apply. Grants are calculated from travel and transport costs of the incoming artists, at a maximum of EUR 25,000 per production and EUR 75,000 per applicant across several productions. The core test is that the foreign work is rarely or never seen in the Netherlands and substantially enriches the existing Dutch offer, which favours experimental, non-canonical and cross-disciplinary programming over mainstream touring. Experimental music and sound-art programming is not excluded; the selection criterion is rarity and added value, not genre. Applications go through the Mijn Fonds portal and there is no fee. Four rounds run each year. TIMING: because the scheme competes against a shared EUR 267,500 per-round pot and assessment takes several weeks after the deadline, organisers should apply at least one full round ahead of the performance date and must not have the activity already underway. Success rate in 2025 was 60 percent of 33 applications.

item.title: Gemeente Utrecht: Project Subsidy Culture (Projectsubsidie Cultuur, round 3 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Utrecht (Municipality of Utrecht)

Location: Activity must have a presentation moment in Utrecht and benefit residents of the municipality of Utrecht. City-restricted by presentation location, not by applicant residence.

Award: Category A: EUR 1,000 to 5,000. Category B: EUR 5,000 to 20,000. No fixed co-financing percentage, but a budget and coverage plan is mandatory. eHerkenning purchase costs may be included in the budget and are reimbursed if awarded. No application fee.

Duration: Single project.

Deadline: 25 Sep 2026

Utrecht's main project fund for cultural activity with a public presentation in the city, covering all art forms including experimental and cross-disciplinary work. Individuals, foundations, associations and companies are all eligible. Two bands apply: Category A of EUR 1,000 to 5,000 assessed on artistic importance and entrepreneurship, and Category B of EUR 5,000 to 20,000 which adds meaning for the city as a third criterion. The activity must be exceptional or innovative, or otherwise of value to the city, its residents or the Utrecht cultural sector; professional projects and amateur, education or participation projects both qualify. Three rounds run each year and the next closes 25 September 2026 at 17:00 CET. TIMING RULE, which catches applicants out: for professional arts applications the presentation may not take place earlier than 13 weeks after the round's closing date, and for participatory applications the project may not start earlier than 13 weeks after that date, so a 25 September 2026 application supports activity from late December 2026 onward. Decisions are issued no later than 13 weeks after the closing date, following review by an independent Adviescommissie Projectsubsidies. Documentation is capped at 15 pages, or 5 pages if a video is included. Applications go through mijnsubsidie.utrecht.nl with DigiD or eHerkenning. Utrecht also runs a rolling Impulssubsidie Cultuur of up to EUR 2,500 for first-time applicants only, open through 31 December 2026.

item.title: BNG Cultuurfonds: Project Grants (round closing September 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting BNG Cultuurfonds (BNG Bank)

Location: Project must take place in Dutch municipalities; projects largely abroad are excluded. Not region-restricted, but 2026 priority goes to Limburg, Overijssel, Drenthe and Zeeland.

Award: EUR 5,000 minimum to EUR 15,000 maximum. The request must represent 5 to 35 percent of total project funding, so at least 65 percent co-financing is required. The fund is never the sole financier, and place-specific projects require at least one local or regional co-financier. No application fee.

Duration: Single project with a clear start and end; must be executed within two years of award. A grantee cannot reapply for 36 months.

Deadline: 27 Sep 2026

BNG Cultuurfonds funds arts and culture projects that add value for Dutch municipalities and their inhabitants, explicitly including temporary exhibitions, public programmes and festivals developed by professional makers. Media art, digital culture and cross-disciplinary work qualify as long as a professional maker's artistic vision leads the project. Only stichtingen (foundations) may apply: no sole traders, associations, individuals, or foundations in formation. Applications go by email to aanvraag.cultuurfonds@bngbank.nl with a signed form, a project plan of at most 3,500 words, a specified budget and coverage plan, current statutes and a recent KvK extract. The grant is EUR 5,000 to 15,000 and can cover no more than 35 percent of the budget. TIMING IS THE MAIN TRAP: for the 27 September 2026 deadline, feedback comes at the end of December 2026 and the project may not start before 1 January 2027, with applications for earlier-starting projects rejected outright with no exceptions. Missing documents are flagged up to one week before the deadline, so anything submitted in the final week cannot be corrected. Plan for roughly four months of lead time. Excluded: amateur art, talent development, education-focused projects, semi-permanent public art, publications, building or renovation, and regular operating costs. Further rounds: 3 January 2027, 28 March 2027, 27 June 2027, 3 October 2027 and 2 January 2028.

item.title: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven: Project Subsidy (Projecten, 2027 round 1)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven

Location: Eindhoven. The applicant must be a legal entity based in Eindhoven and the activity must serve the Eindhoven cultural offering. City-restricted at the applicant level.

Award: Maximum EUR 35,000 per application and maximum 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least 20 percent co-financing is required. No application fee.

Duration: Single project within the 2025-2028 policy period.

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The mid-size project strand of Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven, the arm's-length body that distributes the city's culture budget, and the main municipal route for an Eindhoven organisation to fund a festival, exhibition or public programme. Awards go up to EUR 35,000 and cover a maximum of 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least a fifth of the budget must come from elsewhere. Unlike the Snelgeld strand this route is closed to individuals: only private-law legal entities established in Eindhoven may apply. Rounds run three times a year in fixed windows; the next opens 1 September and closes at 17:00 on 30 September 2026, which is round 1 of the 2027 cycle. TIMING: the decision lag is long by municipal standards at up to 13 weeks after the submission window closes, so a September 2026 application is decided around the end of December 2026 and activity should be planned for 2027. Given Eindhoven's design and technology profile, media-art, design and creative-technology programming fits the remit particularly well. The parallel Snelgeld strand offers up to EUR 5,000 on rolling intake, reopening 1 September 2026 and running until 31 December 2026 or until the tranche budget is exhausted, whichever comes first.

item.title: Mondriaan Fund: Inside-Out Art Museum Residency 2027 (Beijing)
item.description:
Organisation: Mondriaan Fund / Inside-Out Art Museum

Location: Beijing, China. For visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, funded by the Mondriaan Fund.

Award: Subsidy of EUR 8,478 for an artist or EUR 5,622 for a curator/critic toward travel, material and living costs (a 10 percent personal contribution is automatically deducted by the Mondriaan Fund); studio, living space and Inside-Out Art Museum support are paid directly by the Mondriaan Fund. For a selected duo the total is increased proportionally to cover the second applicant's travel and accommodation. Contribution for Caribbean-based residents can be increased for higher travel costs. No application fee.

Duration: Three months: 1 March to 30 May 2027 (flexible start date, set by IOAM in consultation with the resident)

Deadline: 27 Aug 2026

Mondriaan Fund-supported working period at Inside-Out Art Museum (IOAM) in Beijing, one of China's leading independent platforms for contemporary art and research. The museum combines exhibitions, critical inquiry and public programmes, giving residents room for in-depth research, experimentation and exchange within a Chinese art scene that is otherwise hard to access from Europe. The residency is framed as cultural exchange rather than production to deadline: IOAM works with a flexible model that takes the resident's other obligations into account and sets the exact start date in consultation with the selected candidate. WHO: visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. Duos and collaborations may apply (two artists, two curators/critics, or a combination who structurally make work together, submitting a joint plan for the work period that leads to a single result, and who live and work together in the same space during the residency), but each individual must submit a separate application; the apartment is well suited to duos or partnerships. WORK PERIOD: one period of three months, 1 March to 30 May 2027, with room for one artist or duo; you can state a preference for the work period in the application form. Selection is by advisory committee; read the Mondriaan Fund Residency explanation for the conditions, assessment and checklist, plus the fund's general terms and conditions, before applying. DEADLINE: Thursday 27 August 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time / 10:00 Caribbean time.

item.title: Sundance Collab x Merrell: Brand-Supported Storytelling Program 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Sundance Collab (Sundance Institute) in collaboration with Merrell

Location: Online program, open to filmmakers worldwide. Production takes place wherever the filmmaker is based. One participant receives a covered hotel stay at the Sundance Film Festival in Park City, Utah, USA in January 2027.

Award: USD 20,000 production budget per selected filmmaker to make and deliver the greenlit concept, cutdowns (:06, :15, :30) and stills. Includes an online brand-supported storytelling program, and a covered hotel stay for one participant to attend the Sundance Film Festival in January 2027. No application fee.

Duration: Program runs September to December 2026, with an online intensive 30 September to 2 October 2026, production in October, post-production in November and delivery by 14 December 2026.

Deadline: Closed 18 Aug 2026

Sundance Collab and Merrell are selecting five filmmakers from around the world to each make an original 60 to 90 second vertical film for social platforms, built around Merrell's 'It Starts Outside' brand platform. The brief is not a commercial: it asks for a complete, emotionally resonant human story in which the outside acts as a catalyst for change, exploring how stepping outside is an antidote to increasingly screen-locked, indoor lives. Stories should reflect transformation (a moment of reset, reconnection or personal shift), connection (belonging, community, renewed relationship) and human truth (an observed, emotionally grounded moment). The strongest entries show what changed in a person because they went outside, emotionally, physically, mentally, creatively, spiritually or psychologically, rather than a final achievement. Selected filmmakers enter a three-day online intensive in September on collaborating with a brand, then receive USD 20,000 to produce and deliver their greenlit concept, cutdowns (:06, :15, :30) and stills between October and December, with scheduled check-ins. One participant also receives a covered hotel stay to join the team at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2027. APPLICATION: one entry per person; all submitted materials must be created by the submitter; all answers and materials must be in English or carry English subtitles. The core submission is a written response of up to 500 words on how you would approach the brief. CRITICAL GUIDELINES: design for vertical with a strong hook in the first five seconds; prioritise human, observational storytelling over polished commercial aesthetics; feature real people and authentic moments; treat the outside as context rather than the hero; favour everyday, intimate moments over epic outcomes; avoid overt brand narration; no competitor products (Merrell product is provided but must not be the focus); no AI-generated content in consumer-facing materials. Selection criteria are originality, emotional arc, a distinct point of view and cultural relevance. TIMELINE: submissions opened 28 July 2026; deadline 11:59 p.m. PT on Tuesday 18 August 2026 (08:59 CEST on 19 August); selected artists notified by 16 September 2026. An Insider Session with Merrell Creative Director Alex Ho and Sundance Collab Director Patty West runs on 11 August. Sundance Collab provides accommodations and support services for participants with disabilities; email accessibility@sundance.org to arrange services.

item.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Project Subsidy Culture (Projectsubsidie Cultuur, September 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Rotterdam (Municipality of Rotterdam)

Location: Activity must serve a Rotterdam interest and take place in or for Rotterdam. City-restricted by relevance of the activity rather than by applicant address.

Award: No stated per-application cap. Annual pot EUR 1,632,000 split into six rounds of EUR 272,000, with roughly 130 applications per round. Discipline sub-caps: book writing max EUR 4,500; moving image R&D max EUR 4,000; moving-image production max EUR 12,500; post-production max EUR 4,000. Applicants must demonstrably seek other funds or sponsors. Awards over EUR 50,000 require an auditor's statement at reporting, at the applicant's cost. No application fee.

Duration: Single one-off project.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Rotterdam's standing project fund for one-off artistic and cultural activity, and the most accessible municipal route for festivals, exhibitions and public programmes in the city. The discipline list names e-culture outright alongside moving image and artistic film, design and fashion, visual arts and photography, architecture, spoken word and all hybrid forms, so media-art and creative-technology programming is squarely in scope. Both non-profit legal entities and natural persons may apply, so individual artists are eligible. There is no published maximum per application; the real constraint is the EUR 272,000 available per round against roughly 130 competing applications. Six rounds run every year with fixed closing dates on the first of January, March, May, July, September and November. TIMING RULE: the activity may not start until eight weeks after the closing date of the round applied in, so a 1 September 2026 application supports activity from late October 2026 onward. Decisions normally arrive within eight weeks of the round deadline, extendable to 20 weeks. Associations and foundations apply via eHerkenning, individuals via DigiD. Organisations already receiving Rotterdamse Culturele Basis, Cultuurplan, Impulsregeling, national BIS, Lokale Culturele Programmering or a CBK Rotterdam practice contribution are excluded.

item.title: Kunstraad Groningen: Two-Year Programme Scheme (Tweejarige Programmaregeling, 2027-2028)
item.description:
Organisation: Kunstraad Groningen, on behalf of the municipality and province of Groningen

Location: Municipality and province of Groningen. The applicant organisation must be based and active in Groningen. Region-restricted.

Award: EUR 5,000 minimum to EUR 40,000 maximum per year across two years, so up to EUR 80,000 total. Covers a maximum of one third of total project costs, requiring roughly 67 percent co-financing. Annual scheme budget EUR 325,000. No application fee.

Duration: Two years of programming, covering 2027 and 2028.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

This is the Groningen scheme that actually funds festivals, and the correct counterpart to the Kunstraad's Projectenregeling, which explicitly excludes festivals and recurring programmes and redirects them here. It supports coherent, continuous public activity across 2027 and 2028 in all arts and heritage disciplines, naming recurring production series, festivals and programme lines as eligible, with no exclusion of media art, digital culture or experimental sound work. Annually recurring festivals with a year-round paid organisation are explicitly named as eligible applicants. Awards run from EUR 5,000 to 40,000 per year against an annual pot of EUR 325,000, capped at one third of total project costs, so two thirds must come from municipal funds, national funds, box office or own contribution. Unusually, the money may also be used to strengthen the organisation itself on the business side, not only to pay for programme content. The application window is 1 July to 1 September 2026, closing at 23:59, and only applications received on time are processed. Applications must be submitted in Dutch via the Mijn Kunstraad portal with fair-pay standards applied in the budget. Funding covers nothing before 1 January 2027. Professional non-profit organisations only; amateur associations and individual artists are directed elsewhere. Material investments, equipment purchases and housing costs are excluded.

item.title: Canada Council for the Arts: Arts Across Canada and Abroad, Public Outreach (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Canada Council for the Arts

Location: Activities must build audiences and public appreciation of the arts in Canada. Organisations must be incorporated or registered in Canada.

Award: CAD. Minimum and maximum are NOT published publicly; disclosed only in the client portal at arts-services.ca, which requires a login. No application fee. Council funds cannot cover expenses already covered by another revenue source; combined public grants must demonstrate complementarity.

Duration: Project-based; results usually notified within 5 months of the deadline.

Deadline: 14 Oct 2026

Funds activities that build connections between artists and diverse audiences and contribute to public appreciation and enjoyment of the arts in Canada. This is the closest Canada Council fit for running a public programme, a single festival edition, a talks series or audience-facing exhibition programming, as distinct from creating the artwork itself. It is open to arts festivals, presenters and event organisers under the Presenting organization profile, alongside Artistic organizations, Artistic groups and Arts supporting groups, and the profile explicitly includes visual arts festivals, biennials, triennials and quinquennials. Digital arts and new media, media arts, inter-arts, and music and sound art are named among funded practices, so experimental sound art and creative technology programming qualify. IMPORTANT: unlike the Circulation and Touring component, international organisations are NOT eligible for Public Outreach. The Council will not fund projects whose primary focus is educational, therapeutic, recreational or social service delivery, nor fundraising activities or prize and award ceremonies. Deadlines fall twice a year. The related Composite Activities component offers up to 3 years of support for bundled multi-project programmes and may suit a recurring festival arc better.

item.title: The Japan Foundation: Exhibitions Abroad Support Program (FY2027-28 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Japan Foundation

Location: Exhibition takes place at the applicant institution's own venue outside Japan. National rounds run through Japan Foundation offices worldwide.

Award: No published ceiling. Partial-cost grant only: packing and shipping of Japanese exhibits (insurance excluded), catalogue production including digital catalogues, and travel for invited Japanese artists, curators and specialists. Preliminary research and development explicitly excluded. The grant is partial by design, so the host institution funds the balance. No application fee.

Duration: Exhibitions must open between 1 April 2027 and 31 March 2028; results notified April 2027.

Deadline: 01 Dec 2026

The Japan Foundation's flagship grant for organisations abroad mounting an exhibition introducing Japanese art and culture, explicitly covering overseas biennials and triennials that present Japanese artists. It is a partial-cost grant rather than a production budget: it pays toward shipping Japanese works, producing print or digital catalogues, and bringing Japanese artists, curators and specialists to the venue. That cost structure suits media arts, digital culture and art-and-science exhibitions well, where shipping technical work and hosting the artist for installation are the main cost drivers. It is explicitly designed for non-Japanese applicants: museums, galleries and comparable organisations outside Japan. Institutions only, so independent curators and artists cannot apply directly and must be hosted by an eligible institution. Exhibition content must introduce Japanese art and culture, so a Japanese artistic component is mandatory. Recent UK recipients include Tate Modern, the V&A and the Hayward Gallery, so the scheme skews toward established institutions. Applicants are asked to discuss eligibility with the relevant regional arts programme officer before applying. FLAG: full FY2027 guidelines were not yet published by Tokyo headquarters as of July 2026 and this deadline is the funder's own provisional date; reconfirm in autumn 2026.

item.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Helpmann Academy

Location: South Australia (applicant must be a current South Australian resident); funded activity may take place anywhere.

Award: Up to AUD 7,500 per fellowship, three fellowships available. Supported by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. No application fee.

Duration: Funded activity must occur between 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2027

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Three Helpmann Fellowships of up to AUD 7,500 support ambitious, self-directed projects that advance the artistic and professional development of emerging creatives. Fellowships are open across all eligible disciplines, to individuals and to collectives, and funding can go to larger-scale creative projects, tailored professional development, or a combination of both. Previous fellowships have supported the creation of new work, exhibitions and performances, residencies and internships, touring and recording, specialised training, and long-term professional development; each fellowship is shaped by the recipient rather than a fixed programme. ELIGIBILITY IS NARROW AND GEOGRAPHIC: applicants must be current residents of South Australia and either final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, the University of Adelaide, Flinders University, or the University of South Australia. Honours students and graduates (up to five years after the final year of study) are eligible where honours was undertaken directly following the undergraduate degree. Masters and PhD candidates and graduates are not eligible unless they qualify through their undergraduate or honours study. Final-year students may apply provided the funded activity takes place after studies are completed and within the activity timeframe. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning, and level of ambition. The online application requires a CV (max two pages), an official academic transcript, a budget on the Helpmann template, a timeline, project confirmations, letters of support from an academic and an industry referee, and four to six images or one to two audio-visual work samples. An online information session runs 4 August 2026 at 6pm ACST, and the Program Manager, Toni Wills, takes online or in-person application chats (info@helpmannacademy.com.au). Applications opened 15 July 2026 and close 31 August 2026 at 11:59pm ACST, for activity occurring 1 January to 31 December 2027. Free to apply.

item.title: Liveline Fund: Round 1 (UK grassroots live music)
item.description:
Organisation: Liveline, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters

Location: United Kingdom. Guarantorship shows must be at Music Venue Alliance member venues; for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. Regional focus includes the Highlands and Islands, West Wales and Northern Ireland.

Award: No fixed grant sizes published; every application is assessed case by case against a real budget rather than first come first served. The Guarantorship Scheme covers up to 80 percent of losses on a show or tour: if it breaks even nothing is paid, and if it turns a profit the promoter or venue keeps it. The other three funds cover venue hire, travel, accommodation, ferry and remote-access costs, or genre-specific safety, licensing and access costs. No application fee.

Duration: Round 1; applications close Tuesday 18 August 2026

Deadline: Closed 18 Aug 2026

Liveline is a national risk-sharing fund rebuilding grassroots touring, programming and local music scenes across the UK, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters, alongside the LIVE Trust and the industry's voluntary levy on stadium and arena tickets. The premise is that good shows are not happening because the downside risk is too high, so rather than a traditional subsidy it is an incentive-led model that only pays out when things go wrong. FOUR FUNDS: (1) GUARANTORSHIP SCHEME covers up to 80 percent of losses on an individual show or tour, for promoters, in-house bookers, artists or their representatives; break even and nothing is paid, turn a profit and you keep it. (2) LOCAL SCENE DEVELOPMENT FUND covers venue hire costs and local promoter training to build regular programming, for independent promoters or venues developing an in-house programme. (3) TOUR EXTENSION AND REGIONAL ACCESS FUND covers the long travel, fuel, accommodation and ferry costs that stop tours reaching remote parts of the UK, for promoters, agents, management and artists. (4) GENRE SPECIFIC SAFETY AND ACCESS FUND covers extra security, licensing and structural costs for genres and scenes that face additional barriers, for venues, promoters, artists or collectives. ELIGIBILITY: grassroots venues (Music Venue Alliance member venues), independent promoters including AIP members, in-house venue programmers, and artists, agents and teams building sustainable tours. Guarantorship shows must be at MVA subscribed venues, and for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. TWO CATCHES WORTH KNOWING: tours must NOT already be announced, and Liveline funds a headline artist only once. Applications for Round 1 close Tuesday 18 August 2026. Start with the eligibility checker at livelinefund.uk, or contact info@livelinefund.uk.

item.title: ProPublica Emerging Reporters Program 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: ProPublica

Location: Remote, with an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference. RESTRICTED: US citizens or US residents only, and participants must supply a completed W-9 with a valid SSN or ITIN (no exceptions).

Award: $9,000 stipend, paid as two instalments of $4,500 (one at the start of the programme, one at the midpoint), plus a fully funded journalism conference trip with accommodation and expenses covered. No application fee.

Duration: Late September 2026 through June 2027, remote

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

ProPublica's Emerging Reporters Program is a remote mentorship and professional-development programme for aspiring investigative journalists, built specifically for students for whom investigative journalism is financially out of reach. Five students are selected each year. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $9,000 stipend paid in two $4,500 instalments (start and midpoint), one-to-one mentoring from ProPublica journalists, training and resources, and an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference such as the Investigative Reporters and Editors conference (accommodation and expenses covered by ProPublica). ELIGIBILITY: undergraduate juniors or seniors enrolled during the 2026-27 academic year, who can demonstrate financial need and early dedication to journalism through internships, campus publications or local news work. Students from groups traditionally underrepresented in journalism are especially encouraged to apply. HARD RESTRICTION: applicants must be US citizens or US residents and able to file US taxes; the required W-9 needs a valid Social Security number or ITIN, and ProPublica states it makes no exceptions. APPLICATION: resume or CV, current academic transcript, expected graduation date, essays on investigative-journalism interest, career goals, financial circumstances and barriers faced, plus three journalism projects with URLs or PDFs and a backstory of up to 200 words each. Applications close 17 August 2026 at 9:00am ET.

item.title: Trusted Creator Fellowship 2026 (News Creator Corps)
item.description:
Organisation: News Creator Corps (a project of the Good Information Foundation)

Location: Virtual, meeting once a week. RESTRICTED: US-based creators only.

Award: $5,000 stipend on completing the programme. No application fee.

Duration: Roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026, virtual sessions once a week

A short-term virtual fellowship from News Creator Corps that trains independent content creators in the tactical craft of journalism: fact-checking, sourcing and interviewing, applied directly to their own channels during the programme so the community they already serve gets more credible information. It is explicitly not aimed at traditional journalists already trained in reporting fundamentals. STUDENT SEATS: three places in the autumn cohort are reserved for full-time college students aged 25 or younger, who get the same fellowship experience as everyone else. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $5,000 stipend on completion, weekly virtual sessions, and access to discussion forums with the cohort, trainers, staff and alumni. ELIGIBILITY: US-based only. KEY DATES: applications close 17 August 2026 at 11:59pm ET; notifications by the end of September 2026; programme runs roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026. item.title: Terra Foundation for American Art: Convening Grants (Round 1, 2026-27)
item.description:
Organisation: Terra Foundation for American Art

Location: Worldwide. Open to organisations anywhere, but subject matter must relate to the visual arts of the United States or Indigenous arts of North America.

Award: USD 10,000 to 25,000. Administrative costs capped at 20 percent of the grant. No formal match required, but the Foundation prefers not to be sole funder. No application fee.

Duration: Event-based; Round 1 supports programmes taking place after 1 May 2027.

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

The most directly relevant Terra line for organisations running convenings rather than exhibitions: conversations, symposia and workshops that stimulate interdisciplinary and intercultural exchange. Covered costs are unusually broad and practical, including professional fees, artist honoraria, travel, AV support, interpretation and translation, catering, research dissemination, marketing, and administrative costs up to 20 percent. Awards run USD 10,000 to 25,000 and are made twice yearly. The process is two-stage: Round 1 has a grant inquiry due 28 September 2026 followed, if invited, by a full proposal due 30 November 2026, for programmes taking place after 1 May 2027. item.description:
Organisation: European Digital Rights (EDRi), with LSTS at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center

Location: Brussels, Belgium, and online (hybrid). Event on 13 October 2026.

Award: NO speaker fee or honorarium. Where needed, up to EUR 400 per speaker or session organiser towards transport to and accommodation in Brussels, reimbursed against invoices and travel tickets; those with organisational support are encouraged to cover their own expenses. Duration: One-day conference on 13 October 2026. Average session length 50 minutes.

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Privacy Camp holds its 14th edition on 13 October 2026 in Brussels and online, organised by European Digital Rights (EDRi) with the Research Group on Law, Science, Technology & Society (LSTS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center. THEME: 'The Origins of Future Technologies: Towards communities of digital self-determination'. The call starts from the premise that digital futures do not appear from nowhere but are built through land, labour, capital, infrastructure, law, public money, political choices and social struggle, and asks where technologies come from, who gets to shape them, and what conditions make digital self-determination possible. It situates this against the EU's 2026 Tech Sovereignty Package (semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and data centres) and the wider deregulatory agenda including the Digital Omnibus, the AI Omnibus and reforms affecting data protection, privacy, labour and environmental safeguards, asking whose version of sovereignty is actually being discussed. TOPIC AREAS: (1) Material conditions in the production of technologies, covering the natural resources needed across the supply chain (critical components such as semiconductors, water for data centres) and how GDPR, ePrivacy and AI Act safeguards shape the material conditions of AI from data extraction and biometric processing through to data centres, labour and public infrastructure; labour conditions, including who mines critical materials, union-busting across the tech supply chain, and coalitions between tech workers, unions, migrant justice groups, climate movements and digital rights organisations; and capital, meaning the venture capital forces driving the current AI hype and consolidating through defence, security and militarisation. (2) Political vision in the use of technologies, covering military use and how militarisation and securitisation shape the EU deregulation debate, and the political ideologies driving technology development, including what digital self-determination means for communities facing racialised discrimination, surveillance, occupation, border violence, workplace control or environmental harm. (3) Moving technologies forward through communities, covering community innovation for digital self-determination (distributed and self-hosted data storage, AI built by and for community needs, community-led, public or cooperative digital infrastructure); law, deregulation and rights (resisting the Digital Omnibus and specifically the Data Omnibus, defending GDPR and ePrivacy safeguards, protecting access, transparency and automated decision-making rights, enforcing existing digital laws, supporting collective litigation, and challenging the framing of rights as obstacles to EU competitiveness); and building power by connecting grassroots movements across tech worker organising, labour, migrant, LGBTQIA+, climate, economic justice and landback movements. FORMATS: interactive workshops are particularly encouraged, meaning small-group work, peer exchange and collaboration across sectors, coalitions and disciplines, moving from talk to strategic action; panel discussions are also welcome, especially those centring diverse voices and grounded lived experience with room for meaningful audience engagement. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: state a clear objective for the session and what a good outcome would be; make it as interactive as possible; support a diversity of voices and multiple perspectives; average session length is 50 minutes; propose the format that actually suits the idea rather than forcing a panel into a workshop or vice versa. For workshops, make the objectives, structure and facilitation clear and have participants work together in small groups towards a specific goal; the organisers provide additional guidance, support and feedback for workshops. For panels, list a maximum of 4 speakers covering academia, civil society and decision-maker perspectives, and indicate which speakers have confirmed at least in principle. TIMELINE: proposals due via the online form by 10 August 2026 at 09:00 CEST; the Content Committee notifies applicants before 21 August 2026; confirmation to proceed required by 25 August; draft programme published 4 September; speakers and final session description confirmed by 10 September at the latest (earlier confirmation improves the odds that the EUR 400 reimbursement budget covers speaker travel and accommodation); final programme published 28 September. item.title: Wave Hill: 2027 Sunroom Project Space (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill

Location: Glyndor Gallery, Wave Hill, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For early-career artists living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx.

Award: $2,000 honorarium per artist, plus exhibition and professional development support, a co-designed Meet the Artist public program, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. Four artists selected. No application fee.

Duration: Nine to twelve months of research and development leading to a solo presentation during the 2027 season

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

The Sunroom Project Space gives artists in the New York City area who are in the early stages of their careers, regardless of age, the chance to develop and show a site-specific solo project in the Sunroom or Sun Porch of Glyndor Gallery at Wave Hill. For the 2027 season, Wave Hill is especially interested in projects that recognise ancestral wisdom in relation to our connection with the earth and soil: practices, beliefs and values passed down through generations, particularly those that foster harmonious relationships with our ecosystems, for example regenerative farming and agricultural practices and the care of soil, water and plant life. Projects engaging the history of earth or land art (concepts, materials, sites and relationships to place) that intersect with sustainable practices and ancestral wisdom are also welcome. AWARD: four artists are selected for solo presentations, each receiving a $2,000 honorarium, exhibition and professional development support, and nine to twelve months to research and develop their ideas. Each project is accompanied by a Meet the Artist program co-designed with the artist, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. ELIGIBILITY: artists working across media, in the early stages of their career regardless of education, living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx. Not eligible: students enrolled in a degree-granting program; artists with commercial gallery representation; artists who have previously exhibited a site-specific project at Wave Hill; artists who participated in the 2026 Winter Workspace program at Wave Hill. Applications are reviewed by a jury of Wave Hill's Curator of Visual Arts, an invited guest curator and a prior 2026 Sunroom Project Space artist. An online information session is held Monday 13 July, 12-1PM; RSVP to visualarts@wavehill.org with the subject line '2027 Sunroom Project Space Info Session'. DEADLINE: 9 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.
